questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I guess the main aspects and motivating of me choosing Toronto was that I wanted to get outside of Europe and experiencing a different study culture than teh European one. Another motivating was me wanting to visit Canada and I had heard a lot good things about Toronto as a city and UofT in general.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't really all that easy in terms of courses, registration and administrative stuff. You can prep as much as you want, but must of the stuff you kind of had to figure it out on your own, when you got there. That was kind of tough when KU was very strict with the pre-approval on courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I feel like the assistance was all-right. Courses were quite easy for me to get enrolled, but there weren't really any information before I arrived though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is pretty easy to find housing in Toronto as it is a massice city, but everything is insanely expensive. You have to be prepared to pay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The cheapest and most obvious one is Tartu College, so definetely try to get enrolled there, it is very cheap compared to everything else. I did AirBnB which was actually fairly good. There are a lot of options in Toronto, but no cheap ones.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was all right. They were very flexible with dropping courses and enrolling for new ones compared to KU. But it was a bit of a jungle before you arrived.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was all right. They were very flexible with dropping courses and enrolling for new ones compared to KU. But it was a bit of a jungle before you arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The inbound exchange office provided some help, but not a lot. Though they helped me get enrolled to one course, which was quite nice. I just showed up at their office at UofT.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I was able to get about 3 out of 4 of the courses I requested.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get as many courses pre-approved as possible and then select the courses when you get to UofT. It is very easy to enrol and drop courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked my courses at UofT all in all I would say.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses vary from KU in two ways. I guess the workload throughout the semester can be more as there are more assignments and mandatory participation and your grade depend on these things. Quite often the exam is between 20-50 % of the grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was a lot more involving with the students in class I would say. We didn't really have big classes with hundreds of people, which I am used to back home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Microeconomics for policy analysis
Politics in Europe
East European Politics - Topics in comparative politics
Economics of Global Trade

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would say I liked the Eastern European politics course the most as it was probably the most challenging and interesting course I had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You do a lot of stuff while you are on exchange, so just a lot of stuff, but it definetely worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee is pretty cheap compared to DK :). Grocery stores tend to be expensive when it comes to like vegetables, but then all types of meat are very cheap. But most prices are just like Copenhagen all in all.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Oh I did a lot of stuff. I joined the outdoor club, where we were on a trip to Blue Mountains. Then I joined the tri-campus team in soccer, where we won the championship, so that was very nice and a good experience. Besides that I played basketball and joined in as many activities as I could. I reccomend doing the same.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go travel around Canada. Go to Banff as it is beautiful. I went skiing aswell in november. Go to various sports games in Toronto either Uni games or pro sports such as baseball, hockey and basketball. Go to concerts! Chances are your favorite artist plays in Toronto.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Banff, sports, ice-skating, concerts and so on. Even go to New York and of course Niagara Falls.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Canada is probably a good mix between American and European culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them in classes. People are so open-minded as people come from places all over the world.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmmm. People study mostly late-night, which I find very weird. If you go to the study library at like 8-9 pm it is packed in contrast to 9 am, where there are no-one.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just talking to so many different people from all over the world.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Say yes to everything especially the first month. You are bound to make friends and experience so many incredible things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be positive. Try to do everything even though it is expensive. It is definetely worth it in the end. Like go to Montreal aswell.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and just having a different day-to-day life than what you are used to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Hmmmm maybe just being so far away from home from time to time. Not being really close to your family, girlfriend etc. Besides that the exchange stay was a blast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
